his_statement: homotopy category ... S¹ ... no ACU structure
statement: Two assertions occur. First, if the canonical functor G from ordinary suspension localization to monoidal object-inversion fractions is not faithful, no compatible ACU structure making iZ invertible can exist: this conditional follows from the two universal properties. Second, the source asserts that Z=S¹ in the pointed homotopy category supplies such nonfaithfulness. That example is false in the ordinary symmetric-smash setting: the cyclic permutation of (S¹)^⊗3=S³ has degree+1 and is homotopic to the identity, so the symmetric monoidal stabilization theorem applies.

computation.evidence: If a compatible ACU structure existed, the monoidal fraction universal property gives H:P_fraction→P_susp with HG isomorphic to the identity by the ordinary suspension universal property. Thus G is faithful. For S¹, the3-cycle has two transpositions, hence degree(+1) on S³; the self-map is homotopic to identity. This verifies the precise hypothesis of Robalo2.14, not a finite-only analogy.

fate: Robalo2015 Theorem2.14, printedpp445–446, treats an ordinary symmetric monoidal category and its Cat-colimit stabilization: eventual triviality of the cyclic3-permutation gives a symmetric monoidal localization universally inverting the chosen object. There is no finite-CW premise. Applied to S¹ it contradicts the alleged nonfaithfulness example. Voevodsky1998 Theorem4.3, printedp588, gives the earlier ordinary-category theorem. FreydStable1966 §2 pp124–125 fixes the ordinary suspension scope; §4 p137 gives the permutation signs. This does not identify the all-space formal stabilization with the full category of spectra.
